title: Attorney says extended service warranties for used vehicles are waste of money
summary: A news report and attorney describe a customer whose extended warranty company went bankrupt before she could use it, and argue such warranties are rarely worth it.

assertions.quote: THERE IS NO GUARANTEE THE COMPANY WILL BE AROUND WHEN YOU NEED IT

verdicts.note: FTC's scam-warning section says disreputable sellers "may not be in business when you need to use the contract," but for legitimate dealer-sold contracts the guide notes the dealer may have to perform the work if the administrator folds -- so the going-out-of-business risk is concentrated in disreputable sellers, not universal.

assertions.quote: THE DEALS TURN HUGE PROFITS BUT ARE OFTEN LIMITED IN WHAT THEY COVER

verdicts.note: High markups paired with narrow covered-component lists are widely reported and consistent with industry profit-margin data on vehicle service contracts

assertions.quote: BETTER OFF PAYING A FEW HUNDRED DOLLARS BEFORE BUYING THE CAR TO HAVE A MECHANIC INSPECTED, SAVING THE MONEY

verdicts.note: Self-insuring is usually cheaper on average given the negative expected value of warranties, but it depends on vehicle reliability and whether the owner actually keeps the saved money untouched

assertions.quote: ANYONE OWED MONEY MOST LIKELY WILL ONLY GET PENNIES ON THE DOLLAR

verdicts.note: Unsecured consumer creditors in a company bankruptcy are routinely paid a small fraction of claims, consistent with standard bankruptcy priority outcomes
